text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- International High Representative for Bosnia Carl Bildt warns Bosnia's Council of Ministers to urgently adopt the budget for 1997 emphasising that conditions for holding the international donors conference for Bosnia have not yet been met.
- "Mr.Carl Bildt obviously wants to put blame on the Council of Ministers for mistakes that he has made recently," Moslem co-prime minister Haris Silajdzic replies.

- All foreign television agencies will have to leave the Bosnian television building hosting them throughout Bosnian war, by March 31, unless they are members of Eurovision, Bosnian television manager, Amila Omersoftic says.

- Provisional Election Commission of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) is still working on rules and regulations for the September 13 and 14 Bosnia's municipal elections to determine the most effective concept for them, its acting chairman Jerry Robinson says.
- Moslem-Croat federation Forum debates government activities on the establishment of a council for federation implementation and the first report of its media group.

- Bosnian Serb republic President Biljana Plavsic meets the U.S. State Department special advisor William Montgomery and says they agreed that the return of refugees will not succeed without economic assistance.
- The dates for conducting local elections in Bosnia, scheduled for September 13 and 14 are fixed and will not be changed, OSCE chief in Bosnia, Robert Frowick tells a news conference.
- "A hasty mass return of Bosnian refugees from Germany could trigger social and political unrest in Bosnia," Moslem- Croat federation Minister for Refugees, Rasim Kadic, says.

- Because of lobbying and protectionism from its neighbouring countries Bosnia can hardly extend or renew its contracts with the western companies such as Volkswagen, Coca-Cola, Philip Morris and others.

- The World Bank will, this year, take different approach in creation of projects for reconstruction of Bosnia to the one it had last year. It will be much more selective and will focus on financing construction of state institutions and reforms, chief of the bank's office for Europe, Christine Wallich, says.
- President of a Bosnian opposition party and former Bosnian ambassador to Great Britain, Muhamed Filipovic, could be the first Bosnian ambassador to Yugoslavia, according to diplomatic sources.
- 2.7 million German Marks are needed for a full profesional TV coverage of Pope's visit to Sarajevo, Bosnian TV manager, Amila Omersoftic says and asks the government to provide the money.
